questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The country itself and the possibilities to see and explore the country. Iceland is known for it unique nature which was one of the main reason why I choose the place. I also wanted to go somewhere I have never been and I also wanted to get to know a different nordic country. I also have family friends, which was also one of the reasons why I wanted to go to Iceland as I had already heard many great things of the country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Yes I did

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Student housing was easy for me as I applied almost the same day as I got my acceptance letter from RU. I recommend it as it was really nice and close to RU.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is the only available option

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You gain access to mobility online at RU where you have to upload various information and eventually you gain acess to the RU intranet where you can register for courses and apply for the Student ID

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Contacting the International Office was always possible and guides were sent that you could follow.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to be in time and keep track of the deadlines

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Easy level and equivalent to BA

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was similiar to UCPH, but we did not have any seminars where we did presentations and such.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: US Litigation, US legal system, European Human Rights, Climate Law and International Law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: US Litigation and US Legal System. The professor was a really great teacher and made the material easy and interesting to understand.

questions.answer: As expected as Iceland is more expensive than Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There weren't really any and I would have liked to participate in sports such as those offered by KU Studenteridræt

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A law student association which we did participate in and went to event at different businesses and law firms, which was really fun to experience.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: To join all the different events that are organized by ESN and the International Committee at the University of Iceland.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The Icelandic nature and typical Icelandic swimming pools and spas. I highly recommend going on as many trips as possible during weekend. We had a chat for exchange student where you could write about a trip you were planning or join someone who was organizing one.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as it is similar to Denmark

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not really find any cultural differences

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated that the Icelandic culture revolves around enjoying  outdoor activities like swimming in hot springs, hiking and such.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make sure to be in good time with housing, the university organizes introduction days which I highly recommend joining and also a buddy is a great way to get to know the university and have someone to contact if any problems.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To have lived and learned a new culture and to have made friends from many different countries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I did not experience any challenges

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
